blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (E-mail address and display name written to the application log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: log.info("new signup email=%s name=%s id=%s", email, display_name, user_id)
findings.recommendation: Log only the opaque member id (`log.info("new signup id=%s", user_id)`). As written, every sign-up copies the member's e-mail address and display name into the INFO log and wherever logs are shipped and retained; those copies escape the users table, so account erasure and the retention rule never reach them (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 17 erasure). Add a test asserting the log record holds neither the e-mail nor the name.
findings.title: E-mail address and display name written to the application log

findings.recommendation: Drop `email` from the event properties: the proposal's stated purpose is that "Sign-ups are counted in product analytics", which needs no e-mail address (and arguably not even the user id). As written, every sign-up sends the member's e-mail address to the third party at https://beacon.example.com/v1/events (app/analytics.py:5), beyond what the purpose needs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c) purpose limitation and minimisation, Art. 25 by default); the copy at the processor is then out of reach of access and erasure requests (Art. 15, 17). Add a test asserting the tracked properties hold no e-mail.
findings.title: E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS

findings.evidence: """Product analytics, sent to the Beacon SaaS (beacon.example.com)."""
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change introduces Beacon as a new recipient of member data, yet the proposal's Impact and What Changes do not name it as a processor. Confirm a data processing agreement exists (GDPR Art. 28), where Beacon hosts the data and whether that is a transfer outside the EEA (Chapter V), and record it in the plan and the record of processing (Art. 30). Confidence is low: the contract and hosting region cannot be seen from the code.
findings.title: Beacon is a new processor not identified in the plan

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change starts collecting e-mail addresses and display names from self sign-up, but the proposal states neither the lawful basis (Art. 6), nor how long a member row is kept, nor how it is erased (backups included). State them in the proposal; only the controller can decide them, and the users table predates this change.
findings.title: Purpose, lawful basis and retention of sign-up data not stated
